title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Infrastructure Solutions
description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. NVIDIA is seeking an outstanding Senior Software Engineer to join our AI Infrastructure Solutions team in Pune. This is your opportunity to work on groundbreaking technologies and help build the future of computing! NVIDIA is a global leader in innovation, offering a dynamic and inclusive work environment in Pune or equivalent experience. We value diversity and provide equal opportunities to all candidates. If you’re passionate about building scalable AI platforms and autonomous agent solutions that impact industries worldwide, we want to hear from you!

What You’ll Be Doing:
- Design, build, and operate AI infrastructure solutions that power LLM-based applications and autonomous agents across the enterprise.
- Develop agentic AI workflows and multi-agent systems, including tool calling, planning, memory, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and orchestration using frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, or similar.
- Integrate and serve LLMs through APIs and inference endpoints, optimizing for latency, throughput, cost, and reliability.
- Containerize applications with Docker and deploy and scale them on Kubernetes, including Helm charts, autoscaling, and GPU-enabled workloads.
- Take applications to L3 level: own production readiness, advanced troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, performance tuning, and escalation support for complex issues beyond L1/L2.
- Define and maintain observability for AI systems, including logging, metrics, tracing, and monitoring of agent behavior, LLM quality, and system health.
- Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for automated build, test, and deployment of AI applications and infrastructure.
- Develop high-performance backend services and RESTful APIs (Python and/or .NET Core) that expose AI capabilities to internal applications.

What We Need to See:
- Bachelor’s or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
- 5+ years of software engineering experience, with 2+ years working on AI/LLM-based solutions.
- Hands-on experience building agentic AI and autonomous agent systems, including tool use, multi-agent orchestration, and RAG pipelines.
- Strong experience with LLMs and their integration (OpenAI-compatible APIs, NVIDIA NIM, Hugging Face, or similar), prompt engineering, and evaluation.
- Strong proficiency in Python; experience with C#/.NET Core and ASP.NET Core for REST API development is a plus.
- Solid experience with Docker and Kubernetes, including deploying, scaling, and troubleshooting containerized workloads in production.
- Proven experience supporting applications at L3 level, including incident management, debugging, performance optimization, and root-cause analysis.
- Experience with CI/CD tools (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, GitLab CI, Jenkins) and Git-based workflows.

Ways to Stand Out from the Crowd:
- Experience with GPU-accelerated workloads, NVIDIA AI Enterprise, NVIDIA NIM, Triton Inference Server, or NeMo.
- Familiarity with MCP (Model Context Protocol) and agent-to-agent communication patterns.
- Experience with LLM evaluation, guardrails, and safety frameworks.
- Contributions to open-source AI or infrastructure projects.

NVIDIA delivers competitive pay, a wide range of benefits, and the possibility to contribute to groundbreaking technologies. Join us in building the future of computing! Widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers, NVIDIA offers highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package. As you plan your future, see what we can offer to you and your family www.nvidiabenefits.com/

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

description:

title: Senior Software Engineer – Technical Remediation and Enablement - Vice President
description:
The Vice President (VP) / Senior Software Engineer – Technical Remediation & Enablement Lead is a hands-on, code-level technical specialist responsible for driving the direct remediation of software vulnerabilities across enterprise application teams. This individual contributor / team-level technical lead works alongside application developers and contractor engineers to fix static code vulnerabilities (SAST), patch vulnerable software dependencies (SCA/third-party libraries), containerize workloads, and streamline local build/release pipelines to achieve same-day vulnerability hotfix and deployment capabilities.
This role combines active software engineering (writing/refactoring code and debugging pipelines) with technical enablement, guiding squad developers on how to adopt internal security and build tools, resolve tricky dependency conflicts, and package applications into modern containers for rapid, low-risk production releases.

Key Responsibilities & Core Duties
1. Hands-On Code Remediation & Dependency Patching
- Write, refactor, and review application code to directly remediate static code analysis (SAST) findings (e.g., SQL/command injection, cross-site scripting, insecure deserialization, improper error handling, weak cryptography).
- Resolve complex third-party library and framework upgrades (SCA/CVE remediation), managing transitive dependency conflicts, breaking API changes, and version incompatibilities across Java, Python, Go, .NET, or JavaScript/TypeScript stacks.
- Implement targeted automated unit, integration, and regression tests to validate that code fixes and patched libraries do not introduce functional regressions.
2. Containerization & Same-Day Release Enablement
- Work directly in application repositories to write and optimize Dockerfiles, container manifests, and base image configurations (Docker, OCI, Kubernetes/OpenShift).
- Assist application squads in containerizing non-containerized legacy services, establishing minimal base images and automated base-image rebuild triggers for same-day OS/runtime patching.
- Help configure and fine-tune CI/CD build scripts and release pipelines to compress deployment cycle times and eliminate manual deployment steps for emergency hotfixes.
3. Application Plan Technical Validation
- Perform code-level reviews of proposed remediation plans from application teams, verifying whether proposed library version bumps or refactored logic effectively eliminate the root cause of the vulnerability.
- Identify technical prerequisites (e.g., test coverage gaps, build tool upgrades, compiler/runtime updates) needed before a team can successfully patch and release.
4. Contractor Squad Pairing & PR Review
- Act as a peer reviewer and technical guide for external contractor engineers assigned to assist with remediation work.
- Review contractor-submitted pull requests (PRs) for code cleanliness, security correctness, test coverage, and enterprise architectural standards.
- Facilitate smooth technical onboarding and repository access for contractor developers.
5. Internal Tooling Adoption & Developer Feedback
- Actively pilot, adopt, and demonstrate internal developer tools, IDE security plugins, automated PR bots (e.g., Dependabot/Renovate patterns), and local scanning utilities within engineering squads.
- Troubleshoot false positives, scanner configuration errors, and build pipeline failures; provide direct, actionable feedback to internal platform and tooling teams to improve developer experience.

Required Qualifications & Experience
Education & Experience Requirements
- Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, or related technical field.
- 10+ years of hands-on software development and engineering experience delivering enterprise web applications, microservices, or distributed backend systems.
- Proven track record of directly fixing static code vulnerabilities (SAST) and managing third-party dependency/package upgrades in production environments.
- Practical, hands-on experience containerizing applications and working with container orchestration platforms (Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift).

Technical Proficiencies
- Core Programming Languages: Strong, hands-on development proficiency in at least one or two primary enterprise languages: Java (Spring Boot), Python, Go, C#/.NET, or TypeScript/Node.js.
- Static Code Analysis (SAST): Ability to analyze and fix scanner findings from tools such as SonarQube, Checkmarx, Veracode, or Fortify.
- Dependency & Package Management: Practical experience with dependency resolution and build tools: Maven, Gradle, npm/yarn, NuGet, pip/Poetry, or Go modules, alongside SCA tools like Snyk, Black Duck, or JFrog Xray.
- Containers & Runtime: Hands-on experience creating production-grade Dockerfiles, managing multi-stage builds, patching container base images, and deploying to Kubernetes or OpenShift.
- CI/CD & Version Control: Proficient with Git, branching strategies (Gitflow/trunk-based), and pipeline configurations (e.g., Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Tekton, GitLab CI, Harness).

Core Competencies & Working Style
Competency
Behavioral Expectation
Hands-On Craftsmanship
Loves writing code, debugging builds, untangling messy dependency trees, and seeing clean PRs merged to production.
Developer-to-Developer Empathy
Speaks the language of squad engineers, troubleshoots shoulder-to-shoulder, and offers practical solutions rather than abstract advice.
Pragmatic Problem Solver
Able to quickly find safe workarounds or code refactors when direct library upgrades introduce breaking API changes.
Clear Communication
Explains the "why" and "how" of security fixes clearly in PR comments, documentation, and pairing sessions.

Key Performance Indicators (Success Metrics)
- Direct Remediation Output: Number of validated PRs merged and critical/high vulnerabilities (SAST & SCA) successfully resolved across assigned services.
- Same-Day Hotfix Readiness: Number of application components successfully containerized and equipped with automated verification pipelines capable of same-day hotfix releases.
- Turnaround Time for Technical Reviews: Fast, reliable review turnaround for application remediation plans and contractor pull requests.
- Build & Release Optimization: Measurable reduction in build and deployment friction for patched releases within supported application squads.

Education:
- Bachelor’s degree/University degree or equivalent experience
- Master’s degree preferred

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. About the Role

As a Senior Software Development Engineer within HPE's Product Security Office, you will design, build, and scale AI-enabled security applications that improve engineering productivity, security analysis, automation, and decision-making across the enterprise. You will combine software engineering, AI/ML, large language models, agentic workflows, data engineering, and secure development practices to create capabilities that accelerate how Product Security teams identify risk, generate insight, and drive remediation.

- Experience developing applications using the MERN stack and Python. 
- Experience with CI/CD pipelines and tools such as GitOps, Docker, Jenkins, or GitHub Actions. 
- Experience with software systems architecture, including designing and integrating solutions across multiple platform types. 
- Experience evaluating software testing methodologies, developing test plans, debugging complex issues, and creating testing tools and automation. 
- Experience working with AI/ML, cloud technologies, MLOps, large language models, and agentic AI concepts.

- Understanding of AI security, responsible AI principles, and governance frameworks.

title: Intermediate Backend Engineer , Security Factory
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

- Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An Overview Of This Role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in their code by contributing to the static analysis engine that finds them.

Your work spans both the engine and the tools we use to evaluate it. You'll extend how the engine models programs, from parsing source code and resolving symbols to building call graphs and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You'll also build and apply tooling to test its findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, measuring both false positives and missed vulnerabilities.

We build the engine with artificial intelligence (AI) agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. You'll implement component specifications within the team's architecture, working with engineers and AI agents. Good judgment about when to trust agent output, and when to bring it to human review, is central to the role.

What You'll Do

- Extend the program model, including parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis, to support new languages and frameworks.
- Build and apply AI-assisted tooling to implement, review, and validate engine changes and findings, in collaboration with the team's technical leadership. Measure detection quality against known vulnerabilities, judging changes primarily on false positive and false negative rates.
- Develop static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP), along with test fixtures that demonstrate they work.
- Implement component specifications with engineers and AI agents through phased plans and small, reviewable changes. Keep specifications and code in sync.
- Improve the harness, agent instructions, and skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy. Use separate coding and reviewing agents, performance checks, application programming interface (API) checks, and dependency checks, and escalate risky changes to human review.
- Solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity, and identify and address technical debt that slows the team down.
- Write maintainable code that meets our internal standards, and help maintain those standards through code review.
- Participate in on-call rotations to help troubleshoot product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.

What You'll Bring

- Experience using AI or large language model (LLM) tools to generate or evaluate technical content, with the judgment to assess when their output is trustworthy.
- Solid professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Rust or Go. Our engine is written in Rust, the analyzer wrapper in Go, and the monolith integration in Ruby. You'll be willing to work across them.
- An interest in static analysis and application security, including parsing, intermediate representations, taint and data-flow analysis, and how vulnerabilities arise in code. Deep expertise isn't required; we'll help you grow it.
- Organize and progress your work independently in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.
- The ability to communicate technical problems clearly and concisely and propose iterative solutions.
- Helpful but not required: experience with performance optimization, Docker and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), web or mobile frameworks, guardrails for agent-written code such as mutation testing and fuzzing, or program analysis and security research through publications or open source contributions. Willingness to learn performance optimization and containerized workflows is also welcome.

About The Team

The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories. We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules and flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

- Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
- Flexible Paid Time Off 
- Team Member Resource Groups
- Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
- Growth and Development Fund
- Parental Leave 

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.

Privacy Policy: Please review our Recruitment Privacy Policy. Your privacy is important to us.

GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also GitLab’s EEO Policy and EEO is the Law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know during the recruiting process.

description:

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

title: Sr Software Engineer
description:
It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.
Join us to put AI to work for people.

This role is for an engineer to build reliable, maintainable AI-native and cloud-native software. The IC3 engineer works on well-defined features and components with close guidance from tech leads. They focus on developing solid software engineering fundamentals, gaining hands-on experience with modern development practices, and learning to integrate AI/ML services into applications. This role provides mentorship and opportunities to grow technical depth in Java, JavaScript, and ServiceNow platform development while contributing meaningfully to the product.
Responsibility Area: Software Development

• Develop software features and components under the direction of tech leads; take ownership of well-defined, scoped tasks

• Write clean, maintainable code with comprehensive unit tests; follow established coding standards and best practices

• Contribute to the implementation of AI-native features, including prompt design assistance, API integration, and basic evaluation

• Work with assigned features from design through development, testing, and deployment with guidance from teammates

• Troubleshoot and debug issues in development and staging environments; escalate complex issues to tech leads.

• Follow secure coding practices, including responsible handling of customer data and AI safety considerations

• Participate in code reviews and actively incorporate feedback from tech leads.

• Learn and apply CI/CD practices; contribute to automated testing and deployment pipeline

. Effectively leverage AI tools to maximize the daily productivity
Responsibility Area: Learning & Collaboration

• Learn from code reviews, pair programming, and mentorship from tech leads

• Ask clarifying questions and seek guidance when encountering unfamiliar technical challenges

• Actively participate in team discussions, design reviews, and sprint planning

• Communicate clearly about progress, blockers, and technical challenges

• Participate in knowledge-sharing sessions and team learning opportunities

• Support junior teammates and newer developers by sharing what you've learned

• Take initiative to understand the broader system and how your work fits into the product

Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or related field (or equivalent practical experience)

• 5-8 years of professional software development experience

• Proficiency in at least one programming language (Python, Java, or JavaScript); willingness to learn others

• Understanding of fundamental software engineering concepts: version control, testing, debugging

• Basic knowledge of relational databases and SQL

• Familiarity with RESTful APIs and modern web services

• Strong problem-solving skills and ability to learn quickly from feedback

• Good communication skills and ability to work collaboratively with a team

• Understanding of AI/ML concepts; hands-on experience with LLMs or AI APIs a plus

• Prior experience or coursework with ServiceNow platform is a plus

• Experience with Agile development methodologies is a plus

• Ability to take direction, ask for help when needed, and work independently on assigned tasks

. Adherence to software coding practices including owning the code from development to deployment including thorough testing.

• Passion for software quality, testing, and continuous learning

title: Intermediate Backend Engineer , Security Factory
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in their code by contributing to the static analysis engine that finds them.

Your work spans both the engine and the tools we use to evaluate it. You'll extend how the engine models programs, from parsing source code and resolving symbols to building call graphs and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You'll also build and apply tooling to test its findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, measuring both false positives and missed vulnerabilities.

We build the engine with artificial intelligence (AI) agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. You'll implement component specifications within the team's architecture, working with engineers and AI agents. Good judgment about when to trust agent output, and when to bring it to human review, is central to the role.

What you'll do

- Extend the program model, including parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis, to support new languages and frameworks.

- Build and apply AI-assisted tooling to implement, review, and validate engine changes and findings, in collaboration with the team's technical leadership. Measure detection quality against known vulnerabilities, judging changes primarily on false positive and false negative rates.

- Develop static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP), along with test fixtures that demonstrate they work.

- Implement component specifications with engineers and AI agents through phased plans and small, reviewable changes. Keep specifications and code in sync.

- Improve the harness, agent instructions, and skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy. Use separate coding and reviewing agents, performance checks, application programming interface (API) checks, and dependency checks, and escalate risky changes to human review.

- Solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity, and identify and address technical debt that slows the team down.

- Write maintainable code that meets our internal standards, and help maintain those standards through code review.

- Participate in on-call rotations to help troubleshoot product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.

What you'll bring

- Experience using AI or large language model (LLM) tools to generate or evaluate technical content, with the judgment to assess when their output is trustworthy.

- Solid professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Rust or Go. Our engine is written in Rust, the analyzer wrapper in Go, and the monolith integration in Ruby. You'll be willing to work across them.

- An interest in static analysis and application security, including parsing, intermediate representations, taint and data-flow analysis, and how vulnerabilities arise in code. Deep expertise isn't required; we'll help you grow it.

- Organize and progress your work independently in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.

- The ability to communicate technical problems clearly and concisely and propose iterative solutions.

- Helpful but not required: experience with performance optimization, Docker and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), web or mobile frameworks, guardrails for agent-written code such as mutation testing and fuzzing, or program analysis and security research through publications or open source contributions. Willingness to learn performance optimization and containerized workflows is also welcome.

About the team

The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories. We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules and flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world.

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

- Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being

- Flexible Paid Time Off 

- Team Member Resource Groups

- Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan

- Growth and Development Fund

- Parental Leave 

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.

GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also GitLab’s EEO Policy and EEO is the Law.
